top_article.title: People: Barclays IB pivots to co-CEOs, SocGen in shake-up, and more
organisations: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
top_article.summary: Roundup of senior leadership changes across top investment banks, brokers, and market infrastructures. Features Barclays restructuring its Investment Bank under a co-CEO management model to accelerate corporate/market convergence, and Société Générale executing senior executive changes across its Global Banking and Investor Solutions (GBIS) unit. Also tracks appointments and departures at Citi, BofA, Wells Fargo, BoE, Kalshi, Natixis, and the SEC.

top_article.title: Managing the risks of generative AI: a framework for enterprise risk management
top_article.summary: Establishes a practical enterprise risk management (ERM) framework specifically mapping generative AI vulnerabilities onto Basel II operational risk taxonomy. Evaluates hallucination governance, model drift, prompt injection security, and data leakage controls under emerging regulatory standards from the EU AI Act and Basel Committee guidelines.

top_article.title: PRA struggles to follow Fed's FRTB modelling moves
top_article.summary: Market risk and regulatory experts analyze the divergence between US and UK implementations of the Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB). While the US Fed introduced concessions making the Internal Models Approach (IMA) more viable and capital-efficient for systemic dealers, the UK PRA's stricter stance risks driving banks toward the standardized approach, skewing global competitive dynamics.

top_article.title: US rates surge sparks new wave of FX net investment hedging
top_article.summary: Explores how sustained US interest rate differentials have spurred corporate treasurers to launch a massive wave of FX net investment hedging (NIH). Multinationals are increasingly using currency forwards to shield non-dollar balance sheet equity while harvesting positive interest carry, creating record FX forward and cross-currency volumes.

top_article.title: Beyond mirror validation: the cost of ineffective challenge in model risk management
top_article.desk: Model Risk / Journal of Risk Model Validation
organisations: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
top_article.summary: Demonstrates the severe pitfalls of 'mirror validation'—where validators merely re-execute model logic and check discrimination metrics (Gini, KS, AUC) without stress-testing calibration under regime changes. Across 500 simulations of retail credit PD models, mirror validation missed an average 32% underestimation of default probability, triggering an 8.5% loan-level capital shortfall. Presents an adversarial 5-test framework implementing supervisory 'effective challenge' requirements.
